## 0. Choose a layout

| Layout | When | How the pieces find each other |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Inside this monorepo** (fork it, add `examples/my-cards`) | Prototyping; you want the playground with zero setup | npm workspaces |
| **Your monorepo**: `packages/cards` + `apps/server` + `apps/web` | You own the server and the app | Workspaces; `cards` exports `manifest`, `components`, `cards.json` |
| **Separate repos** | Cards shared by several apps / servers | Publish `my-cards` (manifest + components + built `cards.json`) as a package |

The rule that makes all layouts work: **the manifest is pure data and is imported by every side**; the components are imported by browser sides only; `cards.json` is read by the server only.

```
my-cards/
  src/manifest.ts        ← server, view bundle, native hosts, tests
  src/components.ts      ← view bundle, native hosts
  src/cards/*.vue
  src/view.ts            ← entry of the view bundle (runs in the host's iframe)
  src/cards.css
  vite.cards.config.ts   ← builds dist/cards.json
  dist/cards.json        ← the server inlines it into ui:// templates
```

## 1. Install the packages

Until the packages are on npm, use a local path or tarballs (see the README's [Install](../README.md#install)). After the first release:

```bash
npm i @vue-mcp-apps/core @vue-mcp-apps/view @vue-mcp-apps/server
npm i -D @vue-mcp-apps/vite
```

| Side | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| Cards package | `@vue-mcp-apps/core`, `@vue-mcp-apps/view`, `vue`, `@nuxt/ui`, `tailwindcss` · dev: `@vue-mcp-apps/vite`, `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, `@iconify-json/lucide` |
| MCP server | `@vue-mcp-apps/server` (+ `@vue-mcp-apps/core`), your MCP SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/server` v2 or `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` v1), `zod` |
| Native host app | `@vue-mcp-apps/view`, `vue`, `@nuxt/ui` (if the cards use it), your MCP client |

> **TypeScript inside this monorepo.** Workspace packages export their TypeScript sources under the custom condition `vue-mcp-apps:source`. Consumers of built packages need nothing. Inside the monorepo set `"customConditions": ["vue-mcp-apps:source"]` in tsconfig, `resolve.conditions: ['vue-mcp-apps:source', ...defaultClientConditions]` in Vite, and `tsx --conditions=vue-mcp-apps:source` for Node scripts. Never use a bare `source` condition (it collides with third-party packages).

## 2. A cards package

### `package.json`

```json
{
  "name": "my-cards",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    "./manifest": "./src/manifest.ts",
    "./components": "./src/components.ts",
    "./cards.json": "./dist/cards.json"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "build:cards": "vite build -c vite.cards.config.ts",
    "watch:cards": "vite build -c vite.cards.config.ts --watch"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@nuxt/ui": "^4.11.3",
    "@vue-mcp-apps/core": "^0.1.0",
    "@vue-mcp-apps/view": "^0.1.0",
    "tailwindcss": "^4.2.1",
    "vue": "^3.5.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@iconify-json/lucide": "^1.2.0",
    "@vitejs/plugin-vue": "^6.0.0",
    "@vue-mcp-apps/vite": "^0.1.0",
    "vite": "^7.0.0"
  }
}
```

If the package is consumed by a server compiled with `tsc` (not a bundler), export compiled `.js` for the manifest instead of `.ts`, or compile it with your server.

### `src/manifest.ts`

```ts
import { defineCards } from '@vue-mcp-apps/core'

export const cards = defineCards({
  'order-card': {
    title: 'Order',
    description: 'One order with its lines and a cancel button.',
    actions: {
      cancelRequested: { kind: 'tool', tool: 'cancel_order' }, // card-only tool on the server
      opened: { kind: 'link' },
      asked: { kind: 'message' },
    },
    fixtures: {
      paid: { id: 'A-1001', status: 'paid', total: 42.5, lines: [{ sku: 'TEA', qty: 2 }] },
    },
  },
})
export type CardName = keyof typeof cards
```

### `src/components.ts`

```ts
import type { Component } from 'vue'
import OrderCard from './cards/OrderCard.vue'
import type { CardName } from './manifest'

export const components: Record<CardName, Component> = { 'order-card': OrderCard }
```

### `src/cards/OrderCard.vue`

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useCardHost } from '@vue-mcp-apps/view'

const props = defineProps<{ id: string; status: string; total: number; lines: Array<{ sku: string; qty: number }> }>()
const emit = defineEmits<{
  cancelRequested: [args: { id: string }]
  opened: [url: string]
  asked: [text: string]
}>()
const host = useCardHost()
const money = (n: number) => new Intl.NumberFormat(host.hostContext.value.locale, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }).format(n)
</script>

<template>
  <UCard>
    <div class="flex items-center justify-between">
      <p class="font-semibold">Order {{ id }}</p>
      <UBadge :color="status === 'paid' ? 'success' : 'neutral'">{{ status }}</UBadge>
    </div>
    <ul class="text-sm my-3"><li v-for="l in lines" :key="l.sku">{{ l.qty }} × {{ l.sku }}</li></ul>
    <p class="font-bold">{{ money(total) }}</p>
    <div class="flex gap-2 mt-3">
      <UButton color="error" variant="soft" :loading="host.busy.value" @click="emit('cancelRequested', { id })">Cancel order</UButton>
      <UButton variant="ghost" @click="emit('asked', `Why was order ${id} charged ${money(total)}?`)">Ask</UButton>
    </div>
  </UCard>
</template>
```

### `src/view.ts` and `src/cards.css`

```ts
import './cards.css'
import ui from '@nuxt/ui/vue-plugin'
import { startMcpApp } from '@vue-mcp-apps/view'
import { cards } from './manifest'
import { components } from './components'

startMcpApp({ manifest: cards, components, install: app => app.use(ui), appInfo: { name: 'my-cards', version: '1.0.0' } })
  .catch(error => console.error('[my-cards] could not start:', error))
```

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@nuxt/ui";
@source "./cards";
html, body { background: transparent; }
```

`startMcpApp` options: `manifest`, `components`, `install(app)`, `appInfo`, `root` (default `[data-mcp-card]` then `#app`), `card` (default: the root's `data-mcp-card`), `tokens` (host variable → design token map, default `NUXT_UI_TOKENS`), `strings` (per-language overrides of the shell's few words), `displayModes`, `reportClicksToModel` (default `true`).

### `vite.cards.config.ts`

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'
import ui from '@nuxt/ui/vite'
import { defineCardBundleConfig } from '@vue-mcp-apps/vite'
import { cards } from './src/manifest'

export default defineConfig(defineCardBundleConfig({
  entry: 'src/view.ts',
  outFile: 'dist/cards.json',
  cards: Object.keys(cards),
  maxSizeKb: 2048, // fail the build past this
  plugins: [
    vue(),
    ui({
      router: false,                          // no vue-router inside a card; links are actions
      colorMode: false,                       // the host decides light/dark
      icon: { clientBundle: { scan: true } }, // bundle the icons you use: a template fetches nothing
    }),
  ],
}))
```

`cards.json` fields: `generatedBy`, `versions` (vue, @nuxt/ui, tailwindcss, @vue-mcp-apps/view), `sourceHash`, `sources`, `cards`, `script` (one IIFE), `css`. The plugin refuses more than one chunk (no dynamic `import()` in cards) and warns about assets it cannot inline.

## 3. Serve the cards from an MCP server

`createCardServerKit({ manifest, bundle, uriPrefix? })` returns:

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `registerResources(server)` | Registers `ui://cards/<name>` (mime `text/html;profile=mcp-app`, `_meta.ui.csp` from the manifest) for every card that is both declared and built. Returns the URIs. |
| `registerTool(server, name, config, handler)` | `server.registerTool` with `_meta.ui.resourceUri` (+ the legacy flat key) when `config.card` is drawable, and `_meta.ui.visibility` when `config.visibility` is set. `card` / `visibility` are removed before the SDK sees the config. |
| `result(name, props, text?)` | `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text }], structuredContent: { card: { name, props } } }`. |
| `uri(name)`, `html(name)`, `drawable(name)`, `bundle`, `manifest` | Helpers. |

### 3.1 SDK v2 (`@modelcontextprotocol/server`)

```ts
// server/createServer.ts — isomorphic: stdio, HTTP, edge, browser
import { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/server'
import { createCardServerKit } from '@vue-mcp-apps/server'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { cards } from 'my-cards/manifest'

export function createServer(bundle: unknown) {
  const server = new McpServer({ name: 'shop', version: '1.0.0' })
  const kit = createCardServerKit({ manifest: cards, bundle })
  kit.registerResources(server)

  kit.registerTool(server, 'show_order', {
    card: 'order-card',
    title: 'Show order',
    description: 'Show one order as an interactive card.',
    inputSchema: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
    annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },
  }, async ({ id }: { id: string }) => {
    const order = await db.orders.get(id)
    return kit.result('order-card', order, `Order ${id}: ${order.status}, total ${order.total} EUR.`)
  })

  kit.registerTool(server, 'cancel_order', {
    card: 'order-card',
    visibility: ['app'],            // only the card's button; the model never sees it
    description: 'Cancel an order. Called by the card after the user clicks.',
    inputSchema: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
  }, async ({ id }: { id: string }) => {
    const order = await db.orders.cancel(id)
    return kit.result('order-card', order, `Order ${id} cancelled.`)
  })

  return server
}
```

### 3.2 SDK v1 (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`)

The kit is SDK-agnostic (`ServerLike` = anything with `registerTool` and `registerResource`). The only difference is v1's input schema shape (a raw zod shape):

```ts
import { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js'
import { createCardServerKit } from '@vue-mcp-apps/server'
import { z } from 'zod'

const server = new McpServer({ name: 'shop', version: '1.0.0' })
const kit = createCardServerKit({ manifest: cards, bundle })
kit.registerResources(server)
kit.registerTool(server, 'show_order', {
  card: 'order-card',
  description: 'Show one order as an interactive card.',
  inputSchema: { id: z.string() },
}, async ({ id }: { id: string }) => kit.result('order-card', await db.orders.get(id)))
```

### 3.3 stdio

```ts
// server/stdio.ts
import { StdioServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/server/stdio'
import { createServer } from './createServer'
import { readCardBundle } from './bundle'

await createServer(readCardBundle()).connect(new StdioServerTransport())
console.error('[shop] MCP server on stdio') // stdout belongs to the protocol: log to stderr
```

### 3.4 Node http

```ts
// server/http.ts
import { createServer as createHttpServer } from 'node:http'
import { createMcpHandler } from '@modelcontextprotocol/server'
import { toNodeHandler } from '@modelcontextprotocol/node'
import { createServer } from './createServer'
import { readCardBundle } from './bundle'

const bundle = readCardBundle()
const mcp = toNodeHandler(createMcpHandler(() => createServer(bundle)))
const ALLOWED = new Set((process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS ?? 'http://localhost:5173').split(','))

createHttpServer((req, res) => {
  const origin = req.headers.origin
  if (origin) {
    if (!ALLOWED.has(origin)) return void res.writeHead(403).end(`Origin ${origin} not allowed`)
    res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', origin)
    res.setHeader('Vary', 'Origin')
    res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Methods', 'GET, POST, DELETE, OPTIONS')
    res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Headers', 'content-type, accept, mcp-protocol-version, mcp-session-id, last-event-id, authorization')
    res.setHeader('Access-Control-Expose-Headers', 'mcp-session-id, mcp-protocol-version')
  }
  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') return void res.writeHead(204).end()
  if (!req.url?.startsWith('/mcp')) return void res.writeHead(404).end()
  Promise.resolve(mcp(req, res)).catch(() => { if (!res.headersSent) res.writeHead(500).end() })
}).listen(3001)
```

`createMcpHandler` builds a fresh server per request (stateless). Keep state — sessions, stores, caches — **outside** the factory and pass it in (the demo's `createDemoStore()`).

CORS matters only for browser hosts (the playground, a web chat calling your server directly). Desktop hosts and server-side connectors ignore it. Never answer `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on a server that holds anything private.

### 3.5 Express

```ts
import express from 'express'
import { createMcpHandler } from '@modelcontextprotocol/server'
import { toNodeHandler } from '@modelcontextprotocol/node'

const app = express()
const mcp = toNodeHandler(createMcpHandler(() => createServer(bundle)))
app.all('/mcp', (req, res) => { void mcp(req, res) }) // mount BEFORE express.json(): the handler reads the body itself
app.use(express.json())
app.listen(3001)
```

(`@modelcontextprotocol/express` also exists for SDK v2; use it if you prefer its helpers.)

### 3.6 fetch handlers (Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno, Hono)

```ts
import { createMcpHandler } from '@modelcontextprotocol/server'
import bundle from 'my-cards/cards.json' // bundled at build time
import { createServer } from './createServer'

const handler = createMcpHandler(() => createServer(bundle))

export default {
  fetch(request: Request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url)
    return url.pathname === '/mcp' ? handler.fetch(request) : new Response('Not found', { status: 404 })
  },
}
// Hono: app.all('/mcp', c => handler.fetch(c.req.raw))
```

## 4. Reading `cards.json`

| Runtime | How |
| --- | --- |
| Node (tsx, plain ESM) | `JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('../dist/cards.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8'))` — see `examples/demo-cards/src/server/bundle.ts`, which returns `null` (text-only mode) when the file is missing. |
| Node ESM import | `import bundle from 'my-cards/cards.json' with { type: 'json' }` |
| TypeScript `tsc` build | `resolveJsonModule: true` and a static import; `tsc` copies the JSON next to the output. |
| Bundlers (Vite, esbuild, Wrangler) | `import bundle from 'my-cards/cards.json'` |
| Browser (in-page server) | Same import; see `playground/src/project.ts`. |

`asCardBundle(value)` (also used by the kit) accepts the parsed JSON and returns `null` for an empty or malformed one, so a checkout without a build still starts.

## 5. Native cards in a Nuxt 4 app

Your Nuxt app already uses Nuxt UI; the cards render with **your** theme and plugins. No iframe.

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt/ui'],
  css: ['~/assets/css/main.css'],
  // The cards' <UCard>/<UButton> are resolved by Nuxt's auto-import transform; it skips node_modules
  // unless the package is transpiled. (Or import components explicitly: import UCard from '@nuxt/ui/components/Card.vue'.)
  build: { transpile: ['my-cards'] },
})
```

```css
/* assets/css/main.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@nuxt/ui";
@source "../../node_modules/my-cards/src/cards"; /* let Tailwind see the cards' classes */
```

```vue
<!-- components/ToolCard.client.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { McpCard, type CallToolResult, type CardAction } from '@vue-mcp-apps/view'
import { cards } from 'my-cards/manifest'
import { components } from 'my-cards/components'

const props = defineProps<{ result: CallToolResult }>()
const emit = defineEmits<{ message: [text: string]; context: [text: string] }>()
const toast = useToast()
const mcp = useMcpClient() // yours: wraps an MCP Client from @modelcontextprotocol/client

async function callTool(name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>) {
  return await mcp.callTool({ name, arguments: args }) // your server re-checks visibility and auth
}

function onAction(action: CardAction) {
  if (action.kind === 'notify') toast.add({ title: action.message })
  if (action.kind === 'message') emit('message', action.text)   // → send as the user's next chat message
  if (action.kind === 'context') emit('context', action.text)   // → add to the model's next prompt
}

const colorMode = useColorMode()
const hostContext = computed(() => ({ theme: colorMode.value === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light', locale: 'en-US' }) as const)
</script>

<template>
  <McpCard
    :manifest="cards"
    :components="components"
    :result="props.result"
    :host-context="hostContext"
    :call-tool="callTool"
    @action="onAction"
  />
</template>
```

`<McpCard>` props: `manifest`, `components`, `result` (a tool result with `structuredContent.card`) **or** `card` (`{ name, props }`), `hostContext`, `callTool`, `handleLinks` (default `true`: open http(s) links in a new tab), `showStatus` (default `true`). Events: `action`, `result`, `error`. `hostContext` feeds `useCardHost()` inside the card; page styling is yours.

Server-side rendering: cards are interactive widgets; render them client-only (`.client.vue`) unless you have checked every card for SSR safety.

## 6. Native cards in a plain Vue + Vite app

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'
import ui from '@nuxt/ui/vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [vue(), ui({ scanPackages: ['my-cards'] })], // resolve Nuxt UI components inside the cards package
})
```

```ts
// main.ts
import './style.css' // @import "tailwindcss"; @import "@nuxt/ui"; @source "../node_modules/my-cards/src/cards";
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { createRouter, createWebHistory } from 'vue-router'
import ui from '@nuxt/ui/vue-plugin'
import App from './App.vue'

createApp(App).use(createRouter({ history: createWebHistory(), routes: [] })).use(ui).mount('#app')
```

Then use `<McpCard>` as in section 5 (wrap in `<UApp>` for toasts and overlays).

## 7. Your own chat UI

A chat that talks to MCP servers meets two kinds of cards:

1. **Cards you ship** (you have their components): render natively with `<McpCard>`. Wire `call-tool` to your MCP client, turn `message` actions into user turns and `context` actions into notes for the next prompt. This is what Facturador's chat does.
2. **Cards from other servers** (only a `ui://` template): be an MCP Apps host.
   - Copy `playground/public/sandbox.html` (dependency-free) and serve it from **another origin** (a sub-domain, or an opaque `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"` frame when you only have one origin).
   - Use `AppBridge` + `PostMessageTransport` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/app-bridge`; `playground/src/lib/sandboxHost.ts` is a complete reference: handlers for `oncalltool` (with the visibility check), `onopenlink`, `onmessage`, `onupdatemodelcontext`, `onrequestdisplaymode`, `onsizechange`, `onreadresource`, plus message logging.
   - Send plain JSON only (clone reactive state before `sendToolResult` / `setHostContext`).

Decide per tool: `resultCard(result)` returns the card if the result carries one; `getToolUiResourceUri(tool)` (ext-apps) or `tool._meta.ui.resourceUri` tells you whether a template exists.

## 8. Connecting real hosts

**Claude Desktop** — `claude_desktop_config.json` (Settings → Developer → Edit config):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "shop": { "command": "node", "args": ["C:/path/to/server/stdio.js"] }
  }
}
```

With TypeScript sources: `"command": "npx", "args": ["tsx", "C:/path/to/server/stdio.ts"]`.

**VS Code ≥ 1.109** — `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "shop": { "type": "stdio", "command": "node", "args": ["${workspaceFolder}/server/stdio.js"] }
  }
}
```

or `{ "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:3001/mcp" }`.

**claude.ai** — Settings → Connectors → *Add custom connector*, URL `https://your-host/mcp`. For local testing expose `http://localhost:3001` through a tunnel (`cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3001`).

**Goose, MCPJam, Postman, the MCP Inspector** — point them at the stdio command or the HTTP URL. The Inspector: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node server/stdio.js` → *Apps* tab.

## 9. Keeping the bundle fresh in CI

If you commit `cards.json` (so the server needs no build step), add the freshness test from `examples/demo-cards/test/bundle.test.ts`:

```ts
import { sourceHash } from '@vue-mcp-apps/vite'
const bundle = JSON.parse(readFileSync('dist/cards.json', 'utf8'))
expect(sourceHash(ROOT, bundle.sources, bundle.versions)).toBe(bundle.sourceHash)
```

It hashes the sources (CRLF-normalised) plus the key dependency versions, so CI fails when someone edits a card and forgets `npm run build:cards` — without rebuilding minified output byte for byte. If you do **not** commit it, build it in CI before starting or packaging the server (`npm run build:cards`).

## 10. Using the playground with your cards

Edit `playground/src/project.ts` — the only file that names the project under test:

```ts
import { cards } from 'my-cards/manifest'
import { components } from 'my-cards/components'
import { createServer } from 'my-server/createServer'
import bundle from 'my-cards/cards.json'

export const project: PlaygroundProject = {
  name: 'my-cards',
  manifest: cards,
  components,
  createServer: b => createServer(b) as never, // omit to use only Remote mode
  bundle,
  remoteUrl: 'http://localhost:3001/mcp',
  examples: [{ label: 'Order A-1001', tool: 'show_order', args: { id: 'A-1001' } }],
}
```

and point `onBundleUpdate` at your `cards.json` specifier for hot reload. Add your cards' folder to `playground/src/style.css` (`@source`). For the AI demo, the assistant uses whatever model-visible tools your server lists. See [PLAYGROUND.md](PLAYGROUND.md) and [AI_DEMO.md](AI_DEMO.md).

## 11. Migrating a hand-rolled card system

vue-mcp-apps was extracted from Facturador / Hotelier Tools. If your project has a similar system:

| Before | After | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CARD_ACTIONS` (`web/lib/card-host.ts`) | `defineCards({ name: { title, actions } })` | Same idea: event → `tool` / `link` / `notify`; adds `message` and `context`. Payload is now the **first** argument (Facturador used `emit(evt, tool, params)` → `args[1]`). |
| `mountCard(container, tag, props, onAction)` | `<McpCard>` / `CardRenderer` | Vue components, not custom elements; props are real props, not attributes. |
| `web/lib/mcp-app/bridge.ts` | `McpAppBridge` | Same spec messages + `ui/message`, `requestDisplayMode`, `readResource`, `tool-input-partial`, request timeouts. |
| `web/lib/mcp-app/main.ts` | `startMcpApp` | Same flow; host context and theme applied for you. |
| `build-plugin.ts` + `vite.mcp-app.config.ts` → `api/mcp-app/card-app.json` | `defineCardBundleConfig` → `cards.json` (`cards` instead of `tags`, plus `css`, `versions`) | CSS is one compiled stylesheet instead of per-component shadow CSS. |
| `api/mcp-apps.ts` (`registerCardAppResources`, `cardToolMeta`, `adaptCardResult`) | `createCardServerKit` (`registerResources`, `registerTool`, `result`) | Results carry the card directly in `structuredContent`; no adapter pass. |
| `structuredContent.card = { tag, props }`, `ui://remote-component/<tag>` | `structuredContent.card = { name, props }`, `ui://cards/<name>` | Keep old URIs with `uriPrefix: 'ui://remote-component/'`. |
| `mcpAppBundle.test.ts` | `sourceHash` test | Same technique. |

Steps:

1. Move the actions table into `defineCards`, keeping the event and tool names.
2. Convert `.ce.vue` cards to regular SFCs: `defineProps`/`defineEmits`, drop attribute string parsing (`Array | String` props) and shadow-DOM styles; change `emit('approved', tool, params)` to `emit('approved', params)`.
3. Build with `@vue-mcp-apps/vite`; delete the old build plugin.
4. Replace the server's template registration with the kit; replace `adaptCardResult` with `kit.result`.
5. In the app's chat, replace the custom-element mount with `<McpCard>`; keep the server-side allowlist (the kit's `cardTools(manifest)` from core lists every tool a card may call).
6. Run the old and new cards side by side in the workbench (`project.ts`) until they match, then remove the old code.

## 12. Checklist

- [ ] Manifest names are kebab-case; every event the card emits is listed; `tool` actions name real tools.
- [ ] Card-only tools have `visibility: ['app']`.
- [ ] `cards: Object.keys(manifest)` in the bundle config; `cards.json` rebuilt (or built in CI).
- [ ] No secrets in props; links are http(s); no dynamic `import()` in cards.
- [ ] Icons bundled (`icon.clientBundle.scan`), `colorMode: false`, `router: false`.
- [ ] CORS allowlist on HTTP servers used by browser hosts.
- [ ] Workbench: fixture renders in both panes; clicks work in both; Protocol tab shows `tools/call allowed`.
- [ ] Official Inspector `--app-info` reports `hasApp: true` for card tools.


================================================================================
FILE: docs/WRITING_CARDS.md
================================================================================

# Writing cards

A card is a Vue single-file component that:

- **takes props** (its data),
- **emits events** (what the person did),
- **knows nothing about MCP.**

What those events *mean* lives in the manifest. The same file runs inside Claude, VS Code or any MCP Apps host, and natively in your own Vue app.

## Step by step

### 1. Add the card to the manifest

```ts
// src/manifest.ts
export const cards = defineCards({
  'invoice-card': {
    title: 'Invoice',                                   // shown to hosts and in the playground
    description: 'An invoice the user can send or download.',
    actions: {
      sent:       { kind: 'tool', tool: 'send_invoice' },  // the button can only ever run send_invoice
      downloaded: { kind: 'link' },                        // http(s) URL
      questioned: { kind: 'message' },                     // a user message to the chat
    },
    fixtures: {
      draft: { number: 'F-2026-0042', total: 240, currency: 'EUR', status: 'draft' },
    },
  },
})
```

Rules for names:

- Card names are kebab-case with at least one dash (`invoice-card`).
- Event names are the names your component emits (`sent` → `emit('sent', …)`).

### 2. Write the component

```vue
<!-- src/cards/InvoiceCard.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useCardHost } from '@vue-mcp-apps/view'

const props = defineProps<{ number: string; total: number; currency: string; status: 'draft' | 'sent'; pdfUrl?: string }>()
const emit = defineEmits<{
  sent: [args: { number: string }]
  downloaded: [url: string]
  questioned: [text: string]
}>()
const host = useCardHost()
</script>

<template>
  <UCard>
    <div class="flex items-center justify-between">
      <p class="font-semibold">{{ number }}</p>
      <UBadge :color="status === 'sent' ? 'success' : 'warning'" variant="subtle">{{ status }}</UBadge>
    </div>
    <p class="text-2xl font-bold my-3">{{ total }} {{ currency }}</p>
    <div class="flex gap-2">
      <UButton :loading="host.busy.value" :disabled="status === 'sent'" @click="emit('sent', { number })">Send</UButton>
      <UButton v-if="pdfUrl" variant="outline" icon="i-lucide-download" @click="emit('downloaded', pdfUrl)">PDF</UButton>
      <UButton variant="ghost" @click="emit('questioned', `Why is ${number} ${total} ${currency}?`)">Ask</UButton>
    </div>
  </UCard>
</template>
```

### 3. Register the component

Add the card to both component maps:

```ts
// src/components.ts — used by the view bundle and by native hosts
export const components = { 'invoice-card': InvoiceCard, /* … */ }
```

### 4. Return it from a tool

```ts
kit.registerTool(server, 'show_invoice', { card: 'invoice-card', inputSchema: z.object({ number: z.string() }) },
  async ({ number }) => kit.result('invoice-card', await load(number), `Invoice ${number}: 240 EUR, draft.`))

kit.registerTool(server, 'send_invoice', { card: 'invoice-card', visibility: ['app'], inputSchema: z.object({ number: z.string() }) },
  async ({ number }) => kit.result('invoice-card', await send(number), `Sent invoice ${number}.`))
```

`send_invoice` answers with the same card in its new state. The view swaps it in, which is how a card shows "Sent ✓" after the click.

### 5. Build and try it

```bash
npm run dev     # rebuilds cards.json on save; open http://localhost:5173
```

Press the fixture button, edit the props live, then call the tool "as the model" and click through it in both panes.

## Rules

**Props in, events out.**

- A card never fetches, never calls a tool and never reads storage. Everything it shows arrives in props.
- Everything it wants arrives at the host as an event the manifest declared. This keeps cards trivially testable and is the security model.

**The first argument of an event is its payload:**

| Kind | First argument |
| --- | --- |
| `tool` | A plain object: the tool's arguments. |
| `link` | A URL string. |
| `notify` | A message string (optional; `fallback` otherwise). The second argument is optional data. |
| `message` / `context` | A text string. |

**Do not emit reactive state as it is.** Payloads are JSON-copied (`toPlain`) before they cross `postMessage`, so dates become strings and functions disappear. Emit plain data.

**Keep the manifest in sync.** An event the manifest does not list does nothing, silently. If a button "does nothing", check the event name first.

**`useCardHost()` is optional and read-only:**

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `mode` | `'native'` or `'mcp-app'`. |
| `busy` | True while one of this card's tool actions runs. Use it for `:loading`. |
| `hostContext` | Theme, locale, display mode, container size, style variables. |
| `toolInput` | The arguments the model called the tool with. |
| `streaming` | True while those arguments are still arriving (`tool-input-partial`). |

There is intentionally no `callTool` in it.

**Nuxt UI works as usual.**

- `UCard`, `UButton`, `UBadge`, `UCheckbox`, `UProgress`, `UAlert`… are auto-imported by `@nuxt/ui/vite`.
- Use semantic colours (`text-muted`, `bg-elevated`, `text-highlighted`), so host style variables mapped onto Nuxt UI tokens restyle the card.
- Icons must be bundled: `ui({ icon: { clientBundle: { scan: true } } })` plus the `@iconify-json/<set>` package. A template cannot fetch icons from the Iconify API.
- Overlays (`UModal`, `UPopover`) work inside the iframe, but the iframe is only as tall as the card. Prefer inline UI, or request `fullscreen`.

**Fixtures.** Give every card at least one fixture per state (empty, normal, done, error). They are the playground's presets and your tests' inputs.

**i18n.** `hostContext.locale` tells you the host's language (for example `es-ES`). Pick strings from it, or pass already-translated strings in props. The shell's own few words (Loading…, Done.) follow the locale; override them with `startMcpApp({ strings })`.

**Size is automatic.** The view reports its body size on every change. Do not set a fixed height, avoid `h-screen`, and let content define the height.

**Keep cards small and pure.**

- One card is one decision or one view of data.
- Big tables belong in a link to your app.
- Everything a card imports ends up in **every** template (one bundle), so watch heavy dependencies. The build reports the size.

**Never put secrets in props.** Props sit in the conversation and in the host's iframe. A one-time link is a secret: say it in text once, or keep it server-side.

## Testing a card

- **Unit:** mount it with `@vue/test-utils`, pass a fixture, click, and assert on `emitted()`. Outside a host, `useCardHost()` answers `native` with empty refs.
- **Contract:** `cardActionFor(cards, 'invoice-card', 'sent', [{ number: 'F-1' }])` should equal `{ kind: 'tool', tool: 'send_invoice', … }`.
- **Bundle freshness:** `examples/demo-cards/test/bundle.test.ts` recomputes `sourceHash` and fails when a card changed but `cards.json` was not rebuilt. Copy it into your own card package.
- **Three layers:** the playground, or Playwright through `frameLocator('iframe[title="Sandbox proxy"]').frameLocator('iframe[title="MCP App view"]')`.
- **Real hosts:** the MCP Inspector's Apps tab, ext-apps' basic-host, Claude Desktop or VS Code (see the README).


================================================================================
FILE: docs/PLAYGROUND.md
================================================================================

# The playground

The playground has two pages (hash router):

| Route | Page | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#/` | **AI demo** — hero + chat. An in-browser assistant calls the demo server's tools and the cards appear inline in the chat. | Showing MCP Apps the way users meet them. See [AI_DEMO.md](AI_DEMO.md). |
| `#/workbench` | **Workbench** — native pane, three-layer MCP App pane, inspector, controls. | Building and debugging cards. This document. |

Both pages share one MCP connection (in-browser server by default) and are kept alive when you switch, so live views are not torn down. The header has tabs for Demo, Workbench, Docs and GitHub.

The workbench draws the same card twice:

- **natively**, in the page itself;
- **as an MCP App**, inside the three layers a real web host uses.

It also logs every message that crosses between them.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # builds the cards, watches them, serves http://localhost:5173 (#/ demo, #/workbench)
```

Open **http://localhost:5173**, not `127.0.0.1`. The proxy uses the other name; see below.

## The layers

| # | Layer | Where | What it runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **Native** | the page | `<McpCard>` → `CardRenderer` → your `.vue` card, with the page's own Nuxt UI. No iframe, no protocol. |
| 1 | **Host** | `http://localhost:5173` | `AppBridge` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/app-bridge` (the official host bridge) and an MCP `Client` (`src/lib/sandboxHost.ts`, `src/lib/connection.ts`). |
| 2 | **Sandbox proxy** | `http://127.0.0.1:5173/sandbox.html` | `public/sandbox.html`: dependency-free, can be copied into any host. |
| 3 | **View** | `srcdoc` iframe inside the proxy | The template from `resources/read ui://cards/<name>`: your card bundle and `startMcpApp`. |

### Layer 1: the host

`AppViewHost` creates the proxy iframe and connects an `AppBridge` to it through `PostMessageTransport`. It connects before setting `src`, so the proxy's first message cannot be missed. The bridge is created with `null` as its client, so every request from the view goes through playground code that logs it and applies host policy:

| From the view | What the playground host does |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/call` | Allowed only if the tool exists and its `_meta.ui.visibility` includes `'app'`; optionally asks you to confirm. Then forwarded to the server. |
| `ui/open-link` | Opens a new tab. |
| `ui/message` | Appended to the **Conversation** tab. |
| `ui/update-model-context` | Shown in the **Model context** tab. |
| `ui/request-display-mode` | Grants `inline` or `fullscreen`; fullscreen turns the pane into an overlay. |
| `resources/read` | Forwarded to the server. |
| `notifications/message` | Logged. |

Host capabilities advertised: `openLinks`, `serverTools`, `serverResources`, `logging`, `updateModelContext` (text) and `message` (text).

### Layer 2: the sandbox proxy

1. The proxy posts `ui/notifications/sandbox-proxy-ready`.
2. The host answers `ui/notifications/sandbox-resource-ready` with `{ html, sandbox, csp, permissions }`.
3. The proxy creates the inner iframe:
   - `sandbox` as given by the host;
   - `allow` built from `permissions`;
   - `srcdoc` = the HTML with a CSP `<meta>` injected after `<head>`.

   The CSP it builds from `_meta.ui.csp`:

   ```
   default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <resourceDomains>;
   style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <resourceDomains>; img-src 'self' data: blob: <resourceDomains>;
   font-src 'self' data: <resourceDomains>; media-src 'self' data: blob: <resourceDomains>;
   connect-src 'self' <connectDomains>; frame-src <frameDomains | 'none'>; object-src 'none';
   base-uri <baseUriDomains | 'self'>
   ```

4. It relays every other message both ways, untouched. `ui/notifications/sandbox-*` messages are for the proxy only. It never creates requests of its own.

**Two origins from one server.** Vite listens on `127.0.0.1`, so the page can be the host at `http://localhost:5173` while the proxy is loaded from `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. These are two origins, as the spec requires (*Proxy origin: auto / cross-origin*).

On a single-origin deploy such as GitHub Pages, the proxy iframe gets `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"` without `allow-same-origin`. Its origin becomes opaque (`null`), which is still not the host's (*Proxy origin: opaque*).

### Layer 3: the view

The inner iframe's sandbox (*View sandbox*):

- **standard:** `allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms`. This is basic-host's default; the view shares the proxy's origin, which is not the host's.
- **strict:** `allow-scripts allow-forms`. The view gets an opaque origin, with no storage. Use it to check that a card does not depend on `localStorage`.

Chrome warns that *"An iframe which has both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin … can escape its sandboxing"*. That is expected for the standard mode. It is safe here because the frame's origin is not the host's.

## The sidebar

### MCP server

- **In-browser:** `project.createServer(bundle)` is connected to an MCP `Client` through `InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair()`. This is your real server code running in the tab, and it is what the GitHub Pages demo uses.
- **Remote:** Streamable HTTP to a URL (default `http://localhost:3001/mcp`, served by `npm run server:http`). The server's CORS must allow the playground's origin (the demo server reads its allowlist from `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`).

In both modes the client advertises `capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/ui"].mimeTypes = ["text/html;profile=mcp-app"]`.

### Play the model

The example buttons (from `project.examples`) and the tool list:

- **UI** marks tools with a template.
- **app-only** marks tools with `visibility: ['app']`; the model cannot call these.

Pick a tool, edit the JSON arguments (pre-filled from the example, or from the schema's required keys) and press **Call**. The host then:

1. reads the tool's template and re-creates the view;
2. waits for `ui/notifications/initialized` (with a 10 s timeout, which is logged);
3. if *Stream tool input* is on, sends `tool-input-partial` key by key (120 ms apart);
4. sends `tool-input`;
5. calls the tool;
6. sends `tool-result`. On error it sends `tool-cancelled` instead.

The native pane gets the same result.

### Fixtures

Every `fixtures` entry in the manifest becomes a button. Pressing it draws the card from those props without calling a tool: the host reads `ui://cards/<name>`, then sends an empty `tool-input` and a synthetic `tool-result`.

Below the buttons, **Props of `<card>`** shows the current card's props. Edit them and press **Apply to both panes** to re-render both panes. This is the fastest loop for design work.

### Host

| Control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Theme | The playground page *and* `hostContext.theme`. The header's sun/moon button does the same. |
| Locale | `hostContext.locale` (the shell's status words follow it). |
| Host styles | Presets of spec style variables (`hostContext.styles.variables`). The native pane maps them with the same `NUXT_UI_TOKENS`. |
| Display mode | `hostContext.displayMode`; `fullscreen` turns the MCP App pane into an overlay. |
| Proxy origin | `auto`, `cross-origin` or `opaque` (see layer 2). Changing it re-creates the view. |
| View sandbox | `standard` or `strict` (see layer 3). Changing it re-creates the view. |
| Stream tool input | Sends `tool-input-partial` before `tool-input`. |
| Auto-approve tool calls from cards | When off, every card `tools/call` asks you first (`window.confirm`). |

Context changes reach the view as `ui/notifications/host-context-changed` carrying only the changed fields, via `AppBridge.setHostContext`.

The pane header has two buttons: **Cancel** (`ui/notifications/tool-cancelled`) and **Teardown** (`ui/resource-teardown`). A badge next to them shows the last `size-changed` height.

## The inspector

| Tab | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Protocol** | Every JSON-RPC message, newest first. `→` host→view (info colour), `←` view→host (primary colour), `⛨` a host policy decision (allowed / refused / denied, and why), `•` a host-side step (connect, `resources/read`, the model's `tools/call`). Click a row for the full JSON. Filter by layer (`bridge`, `host`, `native`); *hide size/ping* hides the noisy ones. |
| **Conversation** | `ui/message` posts from cards, from both panes. |
| **Model context** | The last `ui/update-model-context`. |
| **Result** | The raw tool result: `content` for the model, `structuredContent` for the view. |

A host that fails to send (typically `DataCloneError`, when a Vue proxy or a function reaches `postMessage`) is logged as **send failed**.

## Hot reload

`npm run dev` runs two things together:

- `vite build --watch` for the card bundle (`examples/demo-cards/dist/cards.json`);
- the playground's Vite server.

When the JSON changes, `project.ts` accepts the update through `import.meta.hot`, and `main.ts` then:

1. swaps the bundle in;
2. reconnects the in-browser server (so templates carry the new script);
3. replays the current run (`tool-input` and `tool-result`) in a fresh view.

The native pane reloads through normal Vue HMR.

## Using it for your own project

Edit **`playground/src/project.ts`**. It is the only file that names the demo:

```ts
export const project: PlaygroundProject = {
  name: 'my-cards',
  manifest: cards,                    // defineCards(...)
  components,                         // { 'my-card': MyCard }
  createServer: b => createMyServer({ bundle: b }) as never, // optional: in-browser mode
  bundle,                             // import bundle from 'my-cards/cards.json'
  remoteUrl: 'http://localhost:3001/mcp',
  examples: [{ label: 'Try it', tool: 'my_tool', args: {} }],
}
```

You also need to:

- Add your cards' folder to `@source` in `playground/src/style.css`, so their Tailwind classes exist in the native pane.
- Update the `import.meta.hot.accept` path in `onBundleUpdate`.

Leave `createServer` out to use *Remote* only. The MCP App pane draws **any** MCP Apps server, even one that does not use this library. The native pane needs your components.

## Deploying to GitHub Pages

```bash
PLAYGROUND_BASE=/vue-mcp-apps/ npm run build    # packages → cards → playground/dist
```

`vite.config.ts` reads `PLAYGROUND_BASE` for `base`. Routing uses hash history, so deep links work on a static host. On `*.github.io` the proxy cannot get a second origin, so *auto* falls back to the **opaque** sandbox. Everything else works the same, including the in-browser server.

## Driving it from tests

The view sits two frames deep:

```js
const view = page
  .frameLocator('iframe[title="Sandbox proxy"]')
  .frameLocator('iframe[title="MCP App view"]')
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Weather in Madrid' }).click()
await view.getByRole('button', { name: 'Refresh' }).click()
```

The inspector rows are `ol li` elements, which is useful for asserting that a given method went by.

# The AI demo

The playground's home page (`#/`) is a chat whose assistant runs **in your browser** and uses the tools of the demo MCP server — which also runs in your browser. It shows MCP Apps the way a user meets them: you ask, a tool runs, an interactive card appears in the conversation, and your clicks on the card flow back to the assistant.

Code: `playground/src/ai/` (`types.ts`, `prompt.ts`, `agent.ts`, `providers/*.ts`) and the demo page in `playground/src/pages/`.

- [What happens in one turn](#what-happens-in-one-turn)
- [Providers](#providers)
- [The decision protocol](#the-decision-protocol)
- [Safety](#safety)
- [Cards in the chat](#cards-in-the-chat)
- [Adding a provider](#adding-a-provider)
- [Running it locally](#running-it-locally)
- [Limits of small models](#limits-of-small-models)

## What happens in one turn

```
you type ──▶ agent.send(text)
              │ turns + model-visible tools + notes from cards
              ▼
          provider.decide(context) ──▶ { action: 'call_tool', tool, arguments }   or   { action: 'answer', text }
              │  invalid / unknown tool / missing args → scripted rules answer, and the chat says so
              ▼
          host check: tool exists and its visibility includes "model"
              ▼
          tools/call on the MCP server  ──▶ result { content (text), structuredContent.card }
              ▼
          card in the chat: resources/read ui://cards/<name> → host → sandbox proxy → view   (or <McpCard> natively)
              ▼
          provider.answerAfterTool(context + tool text) ──▶ one or two sentences
```

Then the card is live:

- a **tool** button (`Refresh`, `Apply 2 of 3`, a vote) goes through the host's `oncalltool` check and may swap the card;
- a **message** button (`Ask what to pack`, `Summarise for the team`) posts `ui/message` → it becomes the next user turn (`fromCard: true`) and the assistant answers it;
- a **context** action (rejecting the approval card) posts `ui/update-model-context` → the text is added to `modelContext` and the model reads it on its next turn ("Notes from cards the user interacted with").

## Providers

| Id | Label | Runs | Needs | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chrome` | Chrome built-in AI | Gemini Nano, on-device, via the Prompt API (`LanguageModel` global) | Desktop Chrome with built-in AI available; the model downloads once (Chrome manages it) | Auto-selected on load when `LanguageModel.availability()` is `"available"`. Uses `responseConstraint` (JSON Schema) for structured output. |
| `webllm` | WebLLM (WebGPU) | An open model compiled to WebGPU, in a Web Worker | WebGPU; ~1–2 GB of disk and VRAM | Models: `Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC` (default, ~1.6 GB VRAM), `Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC` (~0.9 GB), `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC` (~0.9 GB). Downloaded to Cache Storage on first load (explicit click), then instant. `response_format: { type: 'json_object', schema }`. |
| `openai` | OpenAI-compatible | Any `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with tool calling | Base URL, model, optional key | Defaults: `http://localhost:11434/v1`, `qwen2.5:3b` (Ollama). Uses native `tools` + `tool_choice: 'auto'`. The key lives in the tab's memory only. |
| `scripted` | Scripted | Deterministic intent rules | nothing | Always available; the default when nothing else is (e.g. GitHub Pages on a browser without built-in AI). Also the fallback for unusable model replies. Labelled honestly in the UI. |

Status states (`ProviderState`): `unavailable`, `downloadable`, `downloading`, `loading`, `ready`, `error`, with an optional `progress` (0..1) shown in the side panel.

### Enabling Chrome's built-in AI

Recent desktop Chrome ships the Prompt API. If `LanguageModel` is missing or reports `unavailable`, check `chrome://on-device-internals` (model status) and Chrome's built-in AI documentation for your version's flags and hardware requirements. The first `create()` triggers the download; the side panel shows its progress.

### Ollama / LM Studio

```bash
# Ollama: allow the page's origin, then pull a model with tool calling
OLLAMA_ORIGINS="http://localhost:5173,https://juanmandev.github.io" ollama serve
ollama pull qwen2.5:3b
# LM Studio: start the local server (http://localhost:1234/v1) and enable CORS in its settings
```

## The decision protocol

Models without native tool calling (Gemini Nano, small WebLLM models) answer **one JSON object**, constrained by a JSON Schema built from the model-visible tools (`decisionSchema(tools)` in `prompt.ts`):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": { "type": "string", "enum": ["call_tool", "answer"] },
    "tool": { "type": "string", "enum": ["get_weather", "propose_changes", "show_poll"] },
    "arguments": { "type": "object" },
    "text": { "type": "string" }
  },
  "required": ["action"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

Valid replies:

```json
{"action":"call_tool","tool":"get_weather","arguments":{"city":"Oslo","unit":"F"}}
{"action":"answer","text":"Pack a warm coat and waterproof boots."}
```

After a tool runs, `afterToolPrompt` asks for `{"text": "…"}` (`ANSWER_SCHEMA`): one or two sentences about the card, without repeating every number.

### The prompt

`systemPrompt(tools)` lists each tool as a compact signature (`toolSignature`: `get_weather(city: string, unit?: "C" | "F") — description`) plus short rules (when to call which tool, the shape of `propose_changes` and `show_poll` arguments, answer length) and **few-shot examples** — one per offered tool (`USER: weather in Paris → {"action":"call_tool",…}`). `transcript(context)` renders the last 8 turns as text — `USER:`, `USER (clicked a button on a card):`, `ASSISTANT:`, `TOOL <name> RESULT:` — preceded by up to three notes from cards, and ends with *Decide for the LAST user message only: "…"*. Small models follow one block of text better than many short chat turns.

After a tool ran, `afterToolTranscript` sends **only** the latest request and the tool result — with the whole transcript, a 1.5 B model kept re-describing the previous card.

### Argument repair

Small models often pick the right tool but drop arguments (`"Make a poll: cats or dogs?"` → `show_poll({"question": …})` without `options`). When the scripted rules reach the **same** tool and found arguments the model left out, the agent fills them in (`repairArguments` in `agent.ts`) and says so in the chat: *"WebLLM (WebGPU) left out options — filled from your message."* It never changes the tool the model chose, and it never adds a tool call the model did not make.

### Validation (`parseDecision`)

1. Take the outermost `{…}` (models sometimes add prose or code fences — `extractJson`).
2. `answer` needs non-empty `text`.
3. `call_tool` needs a tool **from the model-visible list** and every `required` argument of its input schema.
4. Anything else throws `DecisionError` → the agent notes *"unusable reply (…) — the scripted rules answer instead"* and uses `scriptedDecision`.

The server validates arguments again (zod), and the host re-checks visibility before calling.

## Safety

- **The model sees only model-visible tools.** `modelTools()` filters on `_meta.ui.visibility` including `"model"`; `apply_changes` and `cast_vote` (`visibility: ['app']`) are never offered to it, and the host refuses them if a model names them anyway.
- **Card-only tools need a human click.** The approval card's *Apply* runs `apply_changes` because the manifest maps `approved → apply_changes`; the host's `oncalltool` allows it because its visibility includes `"app"`. Turn off *Auto-approve tool calls from cards* in the workbench to confirm each one.
- **Cards cannot widen their powers.** Whatever a card emits, a tool action runs the declared tool.
- **Everything stays in the browser** for the Chrome, WebLLM and Scripted providers. The OpenAI-compatible provider sends the conversation to the endpoint you typed, and only there; its key is held in memory and never stored.
- **Cards run sandboxed.** In MCP App mode each card is the real three-layer setup (other-origin proxy, `srcdoc` view, CSP from `_meta.ui.csp`).

## Cards in the chat

Each tool call that returns a card adds a chat item `{ role: 'card', card: { tool, args, result, uri, template } }`. The demo renders it:

- **MCP App** (default): an `AppViewHost` (`playground/src/lib/sandboxHost.ts`) per card — official `AppBridge`, sandbox proxy, `tool-input` then `tool-result`; its `onmessage` / `onupdatemodelcontext` are wired to `agent.send(text, { fromCard: true })` / `agent.addModelContext(text)`.
- **Native**: `<McpCard>` with the same result; `message` / `context` actions are wired the same way.

Toggle *Cards as: MCP App | Native* to compare. The side panel's mini log shows the same JSON-RPC messages as the workbench inspector.

## Adding a provider

Implement `AiProvider` (`playground/src/ai/types.ts`) and register it in `PROVIDERS` (`agent.ts`):

```ts
import type { AiProvider } from '../types'
import { afterToolPrompt, ANSWER_SCHEMA, decisionSchema, parseAnswer, parseDecision, systemPrompt, transcript } from '../prompt'

export const myProvider: AiProvider = {
  id: 'mine' as never,             // add the id to ProviderId
  label: 'My model',
  blurb: 'Where it runs and what it costs, in one line.',
  async check() { return { state: 'downloadable' } },            // cheap; never downloads
  async load(onStatus) { onStatus({ state: 'loading' }); /* … */ onStatus({ state: 'ready' }) },
  async decide(context) {
    const raw = await myModel.generate(systemPrompt(context.tools), transcript(context), decisionSchema(context.tools))
    return parseDecision(raw, context.tools)                       // throws DecisionError → scripted fallback
  },
  async answerAfterTool(context) {
    const raw = await myModel.generate('', `${transcript(context)}\n${afterToolPrompt(context.tool, context.resultText)}`, ANSWER_SCHEMA)
    return parseAnswer(raw)
  },
}
```

A provider never touches MCP, the host or a card: it only turns text into a `Decision`.

## Running it locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev                         # http://localhost:5173  (#/ = AI demo)
```

- Use `http://localhost:5173`, not `127.0.0.1` (the proxy needs the other one).
- WebLLM: click *Load* on the provider; the first download takes minutes; later loads come from cache.
- To point the demo at your own server, edit `playground/src/project.ts` — the assistant uses whatever model-visible tools the server lists. Good tool `description`s matter more than anything else for small models.

## Verified runs (2026-10-15, AMD RDNA 3 GPU, Chrome, production build)

| Provider / model | Prompt | Tool call | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WebLLM · Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (load from cache ≈ 2 s, first download ≈ 20 s on a fast line) | What is the weather in Tokyo? | `get_weather({"city":"Tokyo"})` | ~7 s per turn; answer quoted the result correctly |
| WebLLM · Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | Make a poll: cats or dogs? | `show_poll` — model wrote the question, rules filled `options` | Card: *Which is your favorite, cats or dogs?* |
| WebLLM · Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | Propose changing booking #77: 4 guests and add parking | `propose_changes` with both changes | Approve on the card |
| Ollama · qwen3.5:9b (OpenAI-compatible, native tools) | What is the weather like in Lisbon? Use Fahrenheit. | `get_weather({"city":"Lisbon","unit":"F"})` | ~35 s cold start |
| Chrome built-in AI | — | — | Covered by an e2e test with a mocked `LanguageModel` (same API shape); the real model was not available on the test machine |

## Limits of small models

- 0.5–1.5 B models confuse arguments (e.g. put the whole sentence in `city`). Schemas, enums and short descriptions help; the scripted fallback catches the rest.
- Gemini Nano has a small context: the transcript keeps 8 turns and 3 card notes.
- Answers after a tool are deliberately short; the card carries the data.
- The scripted provider recognises the demo's intents only (weather, polls, booking changes, the cards' messages). It exists so the demo never dead-ends, not as an assistant.

# Testing

How this repo tests itself, and how to test **your** cards and servers the same way.

| Level | Where | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Card contract | `packages/core/src/cards.test.ts` | `npm test` |
| Native renderer | `packages/view/src/renderer.test.ts` (jsdom) | `npm test` |
| Protocol conformance | `packages/view/src/bridge.test.ts` (jsdom) | `npm test` |
| Server kit | `packages/server/src/server.test.ts` | `npm test` |
| Bundle freshness | `examples/demo-cards/test/bundle.test.ts` | `npm test` |
| End to end | `e2e/*.spec.ts` (Playwright) | `npm run test:e2e` |
| Types | all packages, example, playground | `npm run typecheck` |
| Official tools | MCP Inspector CLI, ext-apps `basic-host` | see below |

## Unit and protocol tests (Vitest)

`vitest.config.ts` resolves workspace packages to their TypeScript sources (`vue-mcp-apps:source`), so tests need no build. Files that need a DOM start with `// @vitest-environment jsdom`.

### The card contract

Test what a click may do, not how the card looks:

```ts
import { cardActionFor } from '@vue-mcp-apps/core'
import { cards } from '../src/manifest'

it('Apply can only apply', () => {
  expect(cardActionFor(cards, 'approval-card', 'approved', [{ proposal: 'p1', ids: ['c1'], tool: 'drop_db' }]))
    .toEqual({ kind: 'tool', event: 'approved', tool: 'apply_changes', args: { proposal: 'p1', ids: ['c1'], tool: 'drop_db' } })
})
it('unlisted events ask for nothing', () => {
  expect(cardActionFor(cards, 'approval-card', 'deleted', [{}])).toBeNull()
})
```

### Protocol conformance against the official host

`bridge.test.ts` connects our `McpAppBridge` to ext-apps' `AppBridge` + `PostMessageTransport` through two fake windows that deliver messages asynchronously, with `source`, after a real `structuredClone` (exactly what `postMessage` does — which is why reactive proxies fail). It covers the handshake, host context, `tool-input-partial`/`tool-input`/`tool-result`/`tool-cancelled`, `host-context-changed`, `tools/call`, `ui/open-link`, `ui/message`, `ui/update-model-context`, `size-changed`, `ui/resource-teardown`, error propagation and ignoring foreign senders. Copy the `frames()` helper to test a view runtime of your own.

### Server kit against the real SDK

`server.test.ts` builds an SDK v2 `McpServer`, registers cards and tools through `createCardServerKit`, connects a `Client` over `InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair()` and asserts what a host sees: listed resources and their `_meta`, tools' `_meta.ui.resourceUri` / `visibility`, a self-contained template (no `<script src>`, escaped `</script>`), and results with `structuredContent.card`. Do the same for your server:

```ts
const [a, b] = InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair()
await createServer(bundle).connect(b)
const client = new Client({ name: 'test', version: '1' }, { capabilities: { extensions: { [MCP_APPS_EXTENSION]: { mimeTypes: [MCP_APP_MIME] } } } })
await client.connect(a)
const result = await client.callTool({ name: 'show_order', arguments: { id: 'A-1001' } })
expect(result.structuredContent).toMatchObject({ card: { name: 'order-card' } })
```

### Bundle freshness

`bundle.test.ts` recomputes `sourceHash(root, bundle.sources, bundle.versions)` and compares it with `cards.json`; it also checks that every manifest card is in the bundle and that the CSS has no remote `url()` and the script no `import()`. It is skipped when `dist/cards.json` does not exist.

## End-to-end tests (Playwright)

`e2e/` runs Chromium against the playground (built and served by Playwright's `webServer`). The suites cover:

- **Three layers**: a tool call renders the card in both panes; the proxy iframe is on another origin (or opaque); the view initializes; clicks inside the view reach the server (`tools/call allowed` in the inspector).
- **Card actions**: refresh (tool + swap), approval with a card-only tool, voting, `ui/message` into the conversation.
- **Host context**: dark mode reaches the view (`.dark` on its `<html>`).
- **AI chat (scripted provider)**: a typed request produces a card in the chat and an answer; a card's message button produces a new turn.

```bash
npx playwright install chromium   # once
npm run test:e2e
npx playwright show-report        # after a failure
```

Reaching inside a view (two iframes deep):

```ts
const view = page.frameLocator('iframe[title="Sandbox proxy"]').frameLocator('iframe[title="MCP App view"]')
await view.getByRole('button', { name: /Apply 2 of 3/ }).click()
await expect(page.getByText('tools/call allowed')).toBeVisible()
```

Tips:

- Use `http://localhost:<port>` as the page URL so the proxy (served from `127.0.0.1`) is cross-origin; on one origin the playground falls back to an opaque sandbox — test both (`Proxy origin` select).
- Never test the WebLLM / Chrome providers in CI (downloads, hardware). The scripted provider is deterministic.
- `page.addInitScript(() => localStorage.setItem('vma:intro-dismissed', '1'))` hides the workbench intro banner.

## Official tools

```bash
# Does each card tool advertise a template? (exit code 2 when not)
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli npx tsx --conditions=vue-mcp-apps:source examples/demo-cards/src/server/stdio.ts \
  --method tools/call --tool-name get_weather --tool-arg city=Madrid --app-info
# → {"hasApp":true,"toolName":"get_weather","resourceUri":"ui://cards/weather-card","csp":{…},"prefersBorder":false,"resourceMimeType":"text/html;profile=mcp-app"}

# Interactive: Inspector UI → Apps tab
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector npx tsx --conditions=vue-mcp-apps:source examples/demo-cards/src/server/stdio.ts

# ext-apps reference host
npm run server:http &   # http://localhost:3001/mcp
git clone https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps && cd ext-apps && npm i
SERVERS='["http://localhost:3001/mcp"]' npm start   # open http://localhost:8080
```

## Manual checklist for a new card

1. Workbench → *Fixtures* → render each fixture: both panes look the same, light and dark, `es-ES` and `en-US`.
2. Edit props live (empty arrays, long strings, missing optional fields).
3. Click every button in **both** panes; the Protocol tab shows the expected `tools/call` / `ui/open-link` / `ui/message` / `ui/update-model-context` and a `⛨ allowed` line for tools.
4. Switch *View sandbox* to strict (no storage) and *Proxy origin* to opaque: still works.
5. *Play the model* with streaming on; cancel mid-way; teardown.
6. AI demo: ask for it in plain words.
7. Official Inspector `--app-info`: `hasApp: true`.

# CI/CD

All workflows live in `.github/workflows/`. They use Node 22 and `npm ci` (the lockfile is the source of truth).

| Workflow | Trigger | Jobs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ci.yml` | push to `main`, pull requests | install → build packages → build card bundle → bundle freshness → unit/protocol tests → typecheck → build playground |
| `e2e.yml` | push to `main`, pull requests | install → build → Playwright (Chromium) against the built playground → upload `playwright-report/` on failure |
| `pages.yml` | push to `main`, manual dispatch | build with `PLAYGROUND_BASE=/<repo>/` → upload `playground/dist` → deploy to GitHub Pages |
| `release.yml` | tag `v*` | build + test → `npm publish --provenance --access public` for each `packages/*` (only when `NPM_TOKEN` is set) → GitHub release with generated notes |
| `codeql.yml` | push, pull requests, weekly | CodeQL analysis for JavaScript/TypeScript |
| `dependabot.yml` | weekly | npm (root workspaces) and GitHub Actions version updates |

## What each check protects

| Step | Fails when |
| --- | --- |
| Build packages (`tsc -b`) | A package does not compile or its declarations break. |
| Build card bundle | A card fails to compile, the bundle is not one chunk, or it exceeds `maxSizeKb`. |
| Bundle freshness | `cards.json` does not match its sources (relevant when you commit it). |
| `npm test` | The card contract, the protocol conformance against `AppBridge`, the server kit or the renderer regress. |
| `npm run typecheck` | Types break in packages (`tsc -b`), the example or the playground (`vue-tsc`). |
| Build playground | The demo would not deploy. |
| E2E | The three layers, card clicks or the scripted AI chat break in a real browser. |

## One-time setup on GitHub

1. **Pages**: *Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions*. (Or `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages -f build_type=workflow`.) The demo is then at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`.
2. **npm publishing** (optional): create an npm *automation* token and add it as the repository secret `NPM_TOKEN`. Without it, `release.yml` builds, tests and creates the GitHub release but skips publishing. `--provenance` needs `id-token: write`, which the workflow requests.
3. **Branch protection** (recommended): require `CI` and `E2E` on `main`.

## Cutting a release

```bash
# bump versions in packages/*/package.json (and their internal dependencies), update CHANGELOG.md
git commit -am "chore: release v0.2.0"
git tag v0.2.0
git push --follow-tags
```

`release.yml` publishes `@vue-mcp-apps/core` first (the others depend on it), then `view`, `server`, `vite`.

## Running the same checks locally

```bash
npm ci
npm run build:packages && npm run build:cards
npm test
npm run typecheck
npx playwright install chromium && npm run test:e2e
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 PLAYGROUND_BASE=/vue-mcp-apps/ npm run build:playground   # Git Bash on Windows needs MSYS_NO_PATHCONV
(cd playground && MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 PLAYGROUND_BASE=/vue-mcp-apps/ npx vite preview --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4173)   # open http://localhost:4173/vue-mcp-apps/
```

## Using these workflows in your project

- Copy `ci.yml` and replace the build steps with your cards' `build:cards` and your server's build.
- Keep the freshness test if you commit `cards.json`; otherwise build it in CI before packaging the server.
- Copy `e2e.yml` and the `frameLocator` chain from [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) to test your cards inside the three layers.
